Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 6th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on the 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC and the 1st PBUTs performed on the 5H and 6H since Perf. and Squeeze ops were completed on 5/16/22. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Will Dolan and Alyson Marshall. Starting at approx. 10:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Comments: This inspection is taking place as a follow up to IR 3100561 in which violations were issued for an operator reported release on 10/24/2020.It appears that visually impacted material has been remediated (Photo 1, 2, & 5).A roll off box is still on site, the placard on the box indicates that it is associated with this event (Photo 3 & 4).Operator representative Mark Strini was contacted by phone and notified that there appears to be a depression toward the pad berm, where the higher conductivity readings where found, this depression may be acting as a sump (Photo 8 & 9).The sump referenced in IR 3068832 associated with another spill at the site, appears to be on-going.Based on this inspection, violations associated with IR 3100561 will be closed as corrected/abated. Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 07/20/2026, a routine inspection was conducted of the Buffalo Township 1H well. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated on 01/11/2018.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The PCSM BMPs are installed in the locations shown on the approved PCSM plan.- Scouring was observed at the outlet of Cross-Culvert 4 (Photos 15-17). This appears to be resulting in accelerated erosion at the culvert outlet and displacement of riprap apron material approximately 20 feet downslope of the culvert outlet, which appears to be compromising the ability of the riprap apron to reduce stormwater velocity. (Photos 15-17)- The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1). - ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the components required by 78a.55. - The well site was exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage (Photos 14, 18, and 19).- Well 1H appeared to be drilled and equipped for production. The well tag is installed in a permanent and legible manner (Photos 24 and 25). - No obvious fluid leaks or staining that would suggest a leak were observed at or around the gas wells (Photo 23).- The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 20). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photo 22). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to conduct long-term maintenance at the outlet of Cross-Culvert 4, which appears to be resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation.

Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative

Violation Code: 78a55(c) - CONTROL AND DISPOSAL PLANNING – PPC Plan - Containment Practices - Operator’s PPC plan failed to describe the containment practices to be utilized and the area of the well site where primary and secondary containment will be employed as required under 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64a.
Violation ID: 972778
Permit API: 129-29003
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Comments: On August 13, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration inspection of Diversified's Yelenick 2 plugged well following a Well Site Restoration Submission the Department received on 7/22/2025. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 10/24/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 7/24/2025 in accordance with current regulations.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox and locked gate at the plugged well site's access road entrance. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed a Well Control and Disposal Plan as well as an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan. The beginning portion of the access road was observed to be graveled, however the remaining portion of the access road was observed to be restored and exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Upon inspection of the plugged well site, the Department observed the site to be nearing its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement with seed and mulch spread throughout its slightly less vegetated areas. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the vegetatie cover at this plugged well site to ensure it reaches its 70% uniform and adequate cover requirement. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed and no erosion and sediment control features were observed to be installed on site and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the plugged well. A pipeline riser was observed to still be present on site, the Department recommends any equipment not necessary for production of the well be removed from the site.Based on today's inspection, the Well Site Restoration Report submission is being denied due to the access road not being fully restored and the well site not yet exhibiting its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit the WSRR within 60 days after restoration following the instructions for completing form 8000-PM-OOGM0075.In addition, based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging completion.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

Violation ID: 8277570
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Permit API: 125-29184
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Union Township
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 7/15/2025
Comments: On 07/15/2025, a Drilling inspection was conducted at the MINGO WELL SITE in Union Township, Washington County. The Department received a SPUD notification on 06/26/2025 for 15H well (125- 29184). Falcon 25 drilling crew onsite. I was accompanied by EQT drilling site manager Ezekiel. The following was observed during inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) andPreparedness, Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan was present in mailbox (Photo 1).-The well site entrance and access road appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues observed (Photo 2 and 3).-I observed active construction for NINFS004 pipeline along the Mingo limit of disturbance (LOD).Overall, well pad slope and sound wall appeared to be in stable condition (Photo 4 and 5).-Secondary containment was observed throughout well site. Falcon 25 drilling rig, well casings, equipment, drill cuttings were observed within containment. Trucks were onsite to remove impaired water (Photo 6-18).-I observed multiple wet spots along the west side of the drilling secondary containment and throughout the travel lane. I utilized a Field Scout Conductivity probe to observe numerous elevated and over range readings within a 180x70 ft section. The Department contacted Environmental EQT Logan Dominick to notify them of the spill found. The elevated conductivity reading of Over range, 5.46 mS/cm, 6.57 mS/cm, and 11.60 mS/cm was found along secondary containment, truck travel route and in front of operator buildings. I observed the elevated fluid was spread out throughout the well pad within the 180 x 70 ft section. It appears the spill is greater than 42 gallons (Photo 19-25)-The Department reported the spill to EQT Logan Dominick on 07/15/2025 at 9:30 AM. EQT submitted the incident to the Department on 07/15/2025 at 10:40 AM. (CTS 390645)Determination:The operator failed to report the release of impaired fluid with compliance of 78.66 until after the Department inspected and found the spill. Additional photos and documentation are on inspection 2 and 3. Violations are being issued for impaired fluid found by the Department and spilled onto well pad: 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 78a.66(b)(2)

Inspection Date: 2020-02-06
Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:31 in response to a reported release of 15 gallons of glycol from a compressor. I talked with Kellon Balum, Chief, during the inspection. He indicated that free liquid had be removed with a vac truck the previous evening. Equipment was also brought in to remove any visually impacted soil. About 10 cubic yards of soil was removed. After the compressor was brought back online, some remaining glycol left the containment and collected with water in a small sump that was dug near the compressor. A vac truck was brought back to continue to remove the water from the sump as needed. No other issues were noted at the site. All secondary containment appeared to be in good condition and free from excess water. The wells were properly tagged and the cellars filled in with gravel. The site was greater than 70% vegetative cover and appeared stable. It is recommended that the small area of the sump be excavated after no additional glycol collects. The area can then be backfilled and the residual waste disposed of properly. The DEP acknowledges the proper reporting and prompt remediation of the release. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted & Immediately Corrected.

Comments: On 8/16/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Deremer well site. It was 73 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy rainfall has been reported in the region within the last 48 hours and there were water puddles scattered across the pad surface.The Chesapeake company man, Fletcher Brand, explained current operations as follows: A Haliburton frac fleet was on site fracking four newly drilled wells. Three existing wells are shut in but were still staged for production. The frac crew was zippering between the four wells, fracking a stage and jumping to another well. Wireline was staying ahead, prepping the wells ahead of the frac operations. They have completed 37 stages of 327 total stages. Fletcher expects to be onsite another 27 days.Due to fracking requirements at the time of the inspection, Fletcher could not accompany me during the inspection. I started the inspection unaccompanied and was met by the Chesapeake HSE, Chris Bass, as I was viewing the site.I viewed the brine unloading area. Trucks were backed into the station and were being offloaded during the inspection. I field tested water/mud puddles in this area for conductivity with results being at 0.5 mS. Frac and wireline operations were being conducted on plastic lined secondary containment that was protected by drilling mats. The brine tanks were stationed in plastic lined secondary containment. During the inspection, I did witness a 75' x 30' x 1" deep interconnected stream of water puddles on the unprotected pad surface that ran along the south edge of the brine tank secondary containment and continued southeast for approximately 30'. The puddle field tested at 3.13 mS conductance in the approximate center near the southeast corner of the brine tanks. I collected sample 9551-056 from the water puddle for laboratory analysis.I viewed the chemical additive area. Water on the unprotected ground in this area field tested at 0.6 mS conductance or less.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover with steeper sections of the fill slope stabilized with rock. PCSM is addressed on site by four retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.Violations cited in inspection report 3558977 on 5/23/2023 are still outstanding for the site for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.I left the site at 1420 hours.

Comments: On August 22, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022.Precision Drilling Rig 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the 1003H lateral. Precision Drilling has already drilled the 1005H well and have one more well lateral to complete. There were 8 oil based mud tanks, 4 cement tanks, 5 frac tanks and 4 floc water tanks in secondary containment. The containment around the drill rig was in good condition. A vacuum truck is onsite to vacuum up the water in the secondary containment. STL Resources was in the process of pumping out the northwest stormwater vault on the well pad from recent rainfall. The water from the northwest stormwater vault was being pumped into 5 frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter. The water in the southwest stormwater vault was about 6 feet from the top of the vault. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 2 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 33.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 76.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Three monitoring wells have been drilled about 50 yards to the west of the well pad. All the infiltration berms at the site have been hydro seeded. The percent vegetated cover varies from berm to berm. The recently rebuilt northwest and southwest infiltration berms at the well pad are beginning to become vegetated. The water in the northwest infiltration berm was screened for conductivity and resulted in 230 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Violation ID: 1000800

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 7/11/2023
Comments: On July 11, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Present were myself, EQT representatives David Crayne and Carey Vallor-Bell, and Moody representative Jona Stoskey. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on July 10, 2023 at 2:35 PM, and was reported to the Department the same day at 4:27 PM by DJ Hardy. The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Hardy while en route to the pad, who explained that a GPU dumpline failed and spilled approximately one barrel of brine fluid onto the ground. He also stated that the area behind the unit was excavated, but impacted soil remains around and under it. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photo 2). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 3 and 4). GPU units were not placed in secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation, which read 2,360 and 2,750 Microsiemens (see photos 7 and 8). An additional conductivity reading was taken in what appeared to be a brine puddle at the bottom of the excavation, which read above the meter's range (see photo 9). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 12). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 11). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 10). A rolloff dumpster was onsite that appeared to contain the impacted soil that was excavated (see photo 13). According to Mr. Crayne and Ms. Vallor-Bell, SPSI representatives will be onsite promptly to perform further cleanup and to cover the area of impact to prevent spread. Discussions are ongoing within EQT to determine how further remediation efforts will be conducted. Ms. Vallor-Bell stated that this spill will be remediated in accordance with Act 2. When it information is available, the Department requests that the operator provide the following information: - The quantity of what was spilled- How this quantity was obtained- How long was it on the ground- The last time the GPU and associated equipment was tended- Please include photos taken during remediation and the waste manifest

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-14 to Dorso Lp in New Stanton Boro, Westmoreland county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-14
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 877198
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2015-07-10 to Swn Production Co Llc in Jackson Twp, Susquehanna county. 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Swn Production Co Llc
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2015-07-10
Violation Code 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
Violation ID 727629
Permit API 115-21865
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Jackson Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2015-07-10
Comments Afton Sterling, Regulatory Supervisor of Southwestern Energy contacted the Department at 10:25 on 7/10/15 to report a release of (40) barrels of fluid to secondary containment due to a valve popping off on a frac pump truck as a result of over pressure during hydraulic fracturing operations for the Whitehead N 1H well conducted by Baker Hughes Corporation. Impacted areas include the secondary containment liner and berm, fluid transfer line, frac pump trucks, frac equipment, vegetation on the site earthen perimeter berm, soil and rocks on the pipeline Right-of-Way off the pad , and trees below a mulch berm next to the pipeline Right-of-Way off the pad at N- 41° 53' 9"; W- 75° 34’ 33". A white residue was deposited in the impacted areas mentioned, due to the direction of the wind as mist was released from the pop off relief valve on Truck # 2K38. Failure to contain a pollutional substance in a properly lined pit or tank.

Violation(s)
ID: 727629 Date: 2015-07-10 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks. Failure to contain a pollutional substance in a properly lined pit or tank.
ID: 727627 Date: 2015-07-10 00:00:00 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department. Potential for pollutional substances to enter the waters of the commonwealth.
